title: svelte-auth-orchestrator-stream-surface-and-retry-presets
author: Evelyn Park
description: Summary: Introduces a compact 'AuthOrchestrator' surface for TypeScript SDK that centralizes credential rotation, telemetry tags, and a lightweight retry preset family optimized for streaming and low-latency token refresh patterns. This PR also adds explicit stream lifecycle hooks (warmup/drain) to the pullstream surface to improve ergonomic signal points for consumers. Motivation: customers integrate SDKs in long-lived streaming flows; token rotation, backoff tuning, and observability hooks were implemented ad-hoc across languages. This change standardizes behavior and provides small, backward-compatible ergonomics improvements across TS, with companion shims added to Go/Python to preserve parity. What changed (high level): - New AuthOrchestrator class (sdk/typescript/src/auth/orchestrator.ts): encapsulates credential chain, prefetch, and short-circuit fallback profiles. - New retry presets: "fast-fail", "balanced", "latency-optimized" and corresponding config schema in sdk/typescript/src/retry/presets.ts. - Pullstream lifecycle hooks: onWarmup(), onDrain(), and an optional healthHint() in sdk/typescript/src/stream/pullstream.ts. - Telemetry: SDK now attaches standardized tags (auth.source, auth.fallback_used, stream.warmup_ms) to internal spans and metrics. - Backcompat shims: minimal wrapper in sdk/typescript/src/auth/compat.ts to surface previous AuthManager API. - Cross-sdk parity: small adapter implementations added to redwood-sdk-go and redwood-sdk-python directories to keep behavior aligned while preserving idiomatic language surfaces. - Docs: docs/upgrade-auth.md + examples/polylang/ts/stream-warmup.ts updated. - Version bumps: typescript SDK -> 1.7.0, python SDK companion -> 0.9.3 (shim-only), go SDK companion -> 1.4.2 (shim-only). Checklist: - [x] Design doc (ENG-2911) reviewed and linked - [x] TS unit + integration tests added - [x] Go/Python shims added and smoke-tested against staging runtime - [x] Telemetry fields documented - [x] CHANGELOG updated Migration notes: Consumers should: - Prefer AuthOrchestrator where long-lived streams use token rotation; short-lived calls can continue using legacy credential helpers. - Replace ad-hoc setImmediate warmups with onWarmup() when using pullstream helpers for better latency priming. - Use the new 'balanced' retry preset for most streaming workloads; 'latency-optimized' for p99-sensitive realtime routing. Compatibility: Existing APIs remain supported via compat.ts wrappers; calls that relied on internal AuthManager internals might need small refactors. Testing & CI: All CI jobs passed after 2 reruns (flaky e2e due to network emulator). Manual staging test: ran 10k short-lived and 50 long-lived streams concurrently against the staging runtime; observed ~12% fewer token refresh errors and 8% lower median stream warmup time when using orchestrator+balanced preset. Notes: kept the TS surface intentionally small and ergonomic; Go/Python change sets are shim-only and will be expanded in subsequent PRs dedicated to each repo.
commits: 6 commits: 1) introduce AuthOrchestrator and base interfaces; 2) add retry presets and config schema; 3) implement stream lifecycle hooks; 4) compat wrapper and tests; 5) go/python shim adapters; 6) docs and changelog updates
review_comments: Marco Li: Left a couple of inline comments on orchestrator.ts about error bubbling during prefetch; prefer emitting a soft metric and continuing with fallback rather than throwing.
Evelyn Park (author): Updated prefetch handling to record auth.fallback_used and continue; added unit test for fallback path.
Priya Raman: Can we avoid adding another top-level exported class in the main SDK surface? Suggests moving AuthOrchestrator under sdk.auth namespace.
Evelyn Park (author): Moved export to sdk.auth and preserved default import for backward compatibility via compat.ts.
Samir Gupta: Verified telemetry tags in staging; suggested adding stream.warmup_ms as a histogram instead of gauge.
Evelyn Park (author): Switched warmup metric to histogram; updated docs and dashboards.
CI bot: e2e-staging flaky -> rerun triggered; second run passed.
release_notes: TypeScript SDK 1.7.0: new AuthOrchestrator for streaming credential lifecycle, retry presets (balanced/latency-optimized), stream lifecycle hooks (onWarmup/onDrain), telemetry tags for auth/stream. Backwards compatible; small shims added to Python/Go. See docs/upgrade-auth.md for migration steps.
notes_on_migration: - Adopt AuthOrchestrator for long-lived streams to reduce refresh failures; - Use onWarmup to prime KV caches or warm model endpoints; - Swap retry presets conservatively; - No immediate changes required for short-lived blocking calls.
internal_testing_summary: Staging run: 10k short-lived requests + 50 concurrent long-lived streams across 3 regions. Observed reduced auth churn and stable memory profile. e2e flaky job rerun once and passed.
follow_up_tasks: Observability: add dashboard tiles for auth.fallback_used
